idle: (He hums the Mallards fight song and conducts with a hot dog.)
good_ice: Ice like a freshly tuned piano!
bad_ice: That ice is flat. Musically, I mean. Also physically, it isn't.
wet_ice: Wet ice. A diminuendo nobody asked for.
cold: Cold valves on a sousaphone. You've never heard a sound like it. Nobody should.
hungry: Band kids need fries. It's in the budget. The budget is me.
long_line: A queue. Let's all hum. In C.
bored: Is it a key change yet? Somebody change keys.
goal: Hit it, band! No, the other song!
greet_owner: Maestro! Well, you're the owner. Same thing, roughly.
Hello! Don't tell me to keep it down.
leaving_happy: Everyone played in tune! Roughly! Huzzah!
leaving_angry: We'll play the gym. The gym has never told us to keep it down. The gym is too polite.

high_school: From the top, band! Section See, on three!
senior_hockey: Doreen's going up a key. Well. Two can play at that.
figure_show: That music skipped. I felt it in my teeth.

first.say: (A cheerful man carrying a sousaphone case shakes your hand without putting the case down.) Desmond Faulk! Music, Millbrook High. I lead the pep band. And this is the 1971. She's older than the school budget and in better shape.

options.text: Why is there a sousaphone in my lobby?
Great to meet you, Mr. Faulk.

first_tuba.say: Because the band room's flooded and the 1971 doesn't like damp. Also because a lobby is just a concert hall that hasn't been told yet.

first_nice.say: Desmond, please. 'Mr. Faulk' is for students and people asking me to keep it down. You look like neither.

options.text: I'm sorry, Desmond. I'll make it right.
I'll fix it before the next game.

say: Mallards tonight! The band's warming up. Well, the band is warm. The sousaphone is a different story.
(He conducts the warm-up with a rolled programme.) And... strong! Strong! Too strong.

band_plays.say: Listen to that! Section See, full band, every note in roughly the right place! Thank you. The 1971 thanks you. She's never sounded rounder.

say: Maestro! What can I do for you?
Hello! I'm humming in C. Talk in C if you can.

options.text: What do you love about game nights?
You and Doreen have a rivalry?
What do you think of the rink?

job.say: Twenty-four teenagers, eleven instruments that work, and a budget that would embarrass a lemonade stand. I love every minute. Most minutes.

events.say: Mallards games, from Section See, the one with no letter. Lumber Kings when Doreen's on the organ. And a figure show, if the music doesn't skip. A goal on the downbeat is the best sound in the world.

events_see.say: Section C lost its letter years ago. Somebody wrote SEE in pencil, very small. A section that's half a pun is where a pep band belongs.

gossip.say: Doreen goes up a key, I go up a key. She goes up again, I go up again. Last March we ended in a key that doesn't exist. Bernie Ostrowski calls it 'the arms race'. I call it collegial.

rink.say: Wonderful acoustics, if you like echoes, which I do. The stands at Section See are roped off, though. A band can't play standing on a rope.

rink_better.say: Real seats! No rope! The tubas can sit down! Well, tuba. Singular. She's very grateful.

options.text: Louder, if anything. It's a hockey game.
Could you keep it down a little?

do.note: Asked Desmond Faulk to keep the pep band down. He took it hard.

volume_up.say: LOUDER! (He hugs you, sousaphone case and all.) Nobody has ever said that to me. Not once. Not in twenty-two years.

volume_down.say: Keep it down. Yes. Of course. (He hums the fight song very, very quietly, which is somehow worse.)

say: From the top, next game! Bye!
